routing.task_class: Coding Agents state-first continuation, semantic new-task intake, iterative delivery or explicit task-local one-shot planning, evidence-bound capability repair handoff, state audit, and source CLI repair
natural_language_triggers: continue this same repository with a new purpose
the next stage in this repo
routing.primary_route: Use Coding Agents when named or when valid .coding-agents state is paired with strong continuation intent. Inspect active state and completion flags first, semantically preserve and append related progress, and use fresh task_id/epoch/scope only for clearly unrelated work without asking the user for a routine mode. Default coding/source work to ITERATIVE_DELIVERY, which prioritizes a runnable primary-path release and evidence-driven repair. Select non-sticky ONE_SHOT_QUALITY only from an explicit current-task user request and record typed one-shot authority. For a validated source-local capability-improvement proposal, pass its typed artifact reference through intake --evidence-ref. Preserve runner history and dispatch actual workers only through official Codex subagent spawn tools.
fallback_conditions: When official Codex subagent tools are unavailable, keep execution in the parent thread and do not launch a CLI process runner.
non_use_conditions: Mere .coding-agents directory presence and unrelated generic coding, debugging, source changes, delegation, or subagent coordination do not trigger Coding Agents.

interface.default_prompt: Use $coding-agents to inspect this valid .coding-agents state, semantically resume related work with completed progress preserved, use fresh intake only for clearly unrelated work without asking me for a mode, and default coding/source work to ITERATIVE_DELIVERY; use task-local ONE_SHOT_QUALITY only when I explicitly requested it.

inputs.name: Explicit workflow request
inputs.description: A user-named Coding Agents request, strong continuation intent for a repository with valid .coding-agents state, or a request to audit or repair its state or source CLI.

inputs.name: Target repository and workflow identity
inputs.description: The target Git worktree plus task_id, epoch, scope, delivery mode, optional task-local one-shot authority, and optional work type or assignment overlay.

inputs.name: Optional typed evidence reference
inputs.description: One Coding Agents-compatible typed reference, such as a source-local capability-improvement proposal, propagated into standard intake state without granting repair or dispatch authority.

outputs.name: Workflow-state packets
outputs.description: Validated .coding-agents intake, compact shared-contract scaffold, assignment, collection, finalization, orchestration-skeleton, audit, and handoff records carrying the inherited delivery mode.

outputs.name: Official subagent dispatch boundary
outputs.description: Actual workers are dispatched only through official Codex subagent spawn tools; the CLI emits no Codex child process.

outputs.name: Evidence-linked standard state
outputs.description: When intake receives --evidence-ref, project.md, task.md, audit.md, and handoff.md carry the exact validated typed reference.

rules.description: The source CLI records assignments and orchestration skeletons but never launches Codex workers; actual dispatch uses only official Codex subagent spawn tools.

The .coding-agents intake keeps shared scaffold contracts compact and task coverage outcome-focused while assignment, collection, finalization, handoff, doctor, verification, lifecycle, full dispatched-packet contracts, and historical packet compatibility remain enforced.
Fresh intake accepts one optional validated typed --evidence-ref and propagates it to project, task, audit, and handoff state without authorizing repair, dispatch, commit, refresh, or activation.

Codex inspects existing .coding-agents state and completion flags before intake, preserves and appends semantically related progress without asking the user for a routine mode, and creates fresh identity only for clearly unrelated work while preserving historical runner packets.
Successful finalize completes every active-task checklist entry, while doctor and verify-assignments reject finalized/open and all-complete/unfinalized contradictions.

Coding/source work defaults non-sticky to ITERATIVE_DELIVERY; ONE_SHOT_QUALITY requires explicit task-local user-request authority, and task, assignment, handoff, runner, planner, and validator surfaces preserve the selected mode without turning ordinary iterative source changes into exhaustive release gates.
